interpretations.mapping: Operationalize 'presence in a representation' as the free-cell count of the hand-written layout (hand-countable from _layout(): 83 at wall="ring", door="sealed") and 'represented with useful distinctions' as reachable_cells(); their deficit is pocket_cells(). The final's distinction holds in the artifact exactly when pocket_cells() > 0 while those same cells are drawn (as 0.014-high boxes in pocket_color) rather than removed. Read through the probe methods pocket_cells(), reachable_cells(), route_steps() — no pixel reading required.
assumptions: 4-neighbour adjacency (the four cardinal Vector2i offsets in _flood()) is the hall-relevant notion of 'reach'
The character maps returned by _layout() are the whole ground truth: no RNG, so two placements of one token are the same argument (artifact's own header comment)
The amber fill is legible as 'absorbed floor', not merely a third colour
exclusions: No claim about trained embeddings, measured social data, or the hall's own six words — the artifact is a route-level analogy, exactly as the final's exhibit is an authored analogy
No perceptual measurement of the viewer; this interpretation reads counts, not experience

interpretations.mapping: Operationalize 'change one thing' / 'give the region back' as the door axis: at wall="ring", move door from "sealed" to "single", which per _door_cells() frees exactly Vector2i(5, 2) — a '#' in ring row 2, so _door_mattered becomes true. Predicted (labelled prediction, nothing run): pocket_cells() 9 -> 0, reachable_cells() 74 -> 84, route_steps() unchanged at 14, verdict line changing from 'POCKET: %d cells sealed -- filled' to 'every free cell reachable' with no '(the door names open floor)' suffix.
assumptions: apply_grid_config lower-cases and validates against DOORS := ["sealed", "single", "double"], so the string "single" is carried, not silently refused
BFS tie-breaking does not affect route length: with one door and no right-side opening the through-door path dead-ends for y, so the 14-step detour stands
Both setters call _rebuild(), so set order (wall before door or after) cannot mask a value
exclusions: door="double" excluded (second cell Vector2i(4, 2) not exercised)
wall="open" and wall="u_bend" excluded: there the door names cells that are already floor and the axis is declared conditional by the artifact itself
No claim that the route gets shorter; only reach and pocket counts are claimed

interpretations.mapping: Operationalize 'the space available to tell them apart' at its far end as route existence: wall="split", door="sealed" places a full-height '#' column at x=5 (a '#' in all 9 rows of the split layout strings). Predicted from the layout strings alone (nothing run): the flood from x never reaches y, route_steps() returns -1 (the empty-route sentinel, per the method body _route.size() - 1 if not _route.is_empty() else -1), the verdict begins 'NO ROUTE', and pocket_cells() counts y's entire stranded half. The tutorial's continuously measurable separation becomes a binary the program can still measure.
assumptions: The split layout's column 5 is '#' in all 9 rows as written, leaving no gap
-1 from route_steps() is read as 'no route', per the method body _route.size() - 1 if not _route.is_empty() else -1
exclusions: Not part of the bounded comparison below — a second changed condition (wall) would break the one-change rule
No gradual-compression analogue: unlike the hall's COMPRESSION handle, the artifact has no continuous blend export; its walls are discrete shapes
No claim about which half a visitor identifies with

reference_fixture.description: Invented pen-and-paper fixture: the ring board counted by hand from the _layout() character strings in filled_pocket.gd, under door "sealed" and then door "single". Every number below is derived from the .gd alone; none is taken from the registry description, any measured_* block, or any past probe or capture. Where a derived number happens to coincide with a registry phrase (the interior is 9 cells there too, and the registry's measured U-route cost of 14 equals the ring route derived here, because ring and u_bend share every route-blocking cell outside the mouth — each pair describes one hand-written layout), the authority here is the shown arithmetic. All expected values are PREDICTIONS: nothing has run under this record's identity.
constants_cited: _at(): x = (p.x - (W-1)*0.5) * cell, z = (p.y - (H-1)*0.5) * cell; start/goal spheres placed at _at(e, 0.016)
expected: PREDICTION (sealed baseline): route_steps() == 14, pocket_cells() == 9, reachable_cells() == 74; plate reads 'ROUTE: 14 steps' + 'POCKET: 9 cells sealed -- filled'

PREDICTION (door "single"): route_steps() == 14, pocket_cells() == 0, reachable_cells() == 84; plate reads 'ROUTE: 14 steps' + 'every free cell reachable', with NO '(the door names open floor)' line because _door_mattered is true at ring
PREDICTION (geometry): the x marker's local position is (-0.18, 0.016, -0.036) metres
reference_fixture.arithmetic: Board: W*H = 11*9 = 99 cells. Ring walls counted off the layout strings: row2 has 5 '#' (cols 3-7), rows 3-5 have 2 each (cols 3 and 7), row6 has 5 -> 5+2+2+2+5 = 16 walls; free = 99-16 = 83. Enclosed interior = cols 4-6 x rows 3-5 = 3*3 = 9 free cells walled on all four sides, so the flood from x(0,3) reaches 83-9 = 74 and pocket = 9. Route: row 3 is blocked at (3,3)/(7,3) and row 2 at cols 3-7, so any x->y path must cross on row 1 (or symmetrically row 7): >= 2 vertical up + >= 10 horizontal + >= 2 vertical down = >= 14; achieved by (0,3)->(2,3)->(2,1)->(8,1)->(8,3)->(10,3) = 2+2+6+2+2 = 14, so BFS route_steps = 14 regardless of tie-breaking. Door "single" frees (5,2): walls 16-1 = 15, free 83+1 = 84; the interior drains through (5,2)->(5,1), so reachable = 84 and pocket = 0; with no second opening in the right wall the through-door path dead-ends for y, so the route stays 14. Marker: _at(Vector2i(0,3), 0.016) gives x = (0-5)*0.036 = -0.18, z = (3-4)*0.036 = -0.036.

questions.question: Can the hall's predict-then-check discipline be carried from authored gaps to authored reachability: from the hand-written character map alone, predict before anything runs how many steps the route from x to y costs and how many free cells the flood will never reach, then change exactly one authored cell and predict again?

What does the encounter become at the limit the hall's slider never reaches — when a region of the map remains present, coloured and in place, yet no route arrives: does a visitor meet those cells as floor or as wall, and does opening a single door give the region back without any cell's occupancy changing?

reconsider_if: A hand recount of the ring layout gives counts other than 16 wall / 83 free / 9 interior, or a shorter-than-14 route is exhibited — the whole fixture is then wrong and must be rebuilt before any run is scored against it.

A live probe at wall="ring" disagrees with the fixture (e.g. door "single" fails to drain the pocket) — test the handoff before the artifact, per the registry's own what_to_do_if_it_measures_lower: check _rejects.json and setter order before concluding anything about the design.

The hall texts are revised to mention filled_pocket (tutorial.md is already dirty in the working tree) — the binding's premise that the texts predate the artifact fails, and both excerpts must be re-selected against the new bytes.

In the headset the amber pocket reads as decoration or a third team colour rather than 'floor absorbed into wall' — the final-role encounter question is then unresolved, and a rendering interpretation (height, emission, or the plate's wording) becomes its own experiment rather than a repair.

The flood's neighbour set changes (e.g. diagonals added) or _layout() is edited — 'reach' no longer matches the hall's floor metaphor as mapped, and all three interpretations need remapping, not just renumbering.
